mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in periods of declining FEDFUNDS is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 0.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in employment (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days through a joint labor market signal.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative coefficient with p > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (defined by quarterly GDP level above 13000 billion and monthly housing starts above 600 thousand units), the S&P 500 exhibits positive forward returns as investors anticipate peak economic activity before a potential slowdown, with the regime being active when both GDPC1 and HOUST exceed their respective thresholds.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime (GDPC1 > 13000 and HOUST > 600), the S&P 500 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 10.0%, it signals an impending economic downturn that reduces corporate profits and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 10.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO) combined with falling inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a healthy supply response to demand and easing price pressures, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days through a joint supply-inflation signal.
failure_condition: The joint signal of INDPRO rising and CPIAUCSL falling fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative coefficient with p > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing retail sales (RSAFS) reflect strong consumer demand that supports corporate revenue growth and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific threshold conditions.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for RSAFS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return in periods of rising RSAFS is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 0.5% and CPIAUCSL above 2.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as higher interest rates and persistent inflation pressure equity valuations, resulting in negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the monetary tightening cycle regime (FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 2.0), the S&P 500 fails to produce negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.
